# PR #1222 — Round-2 FULL-PR adversarial review

**Range:** head `b07b315` vs merge-base `f57df191` (clean — merge-base already includes #1216/#1217, so **no merged-main noise**; all 9 files are PR work). **All 5 CI runs verified:** dispatches `28712987067`(CI)/`28712447278`(Backtester) green at `b07b315`; red proof `28711599503` failure at `3e963dbb`; PR-event `28713372515`/`28713372595` green.

**Round-1 F1 is fixed and verified. The four round-2 changes all do what the packet claims.** Two residual findings, both about the *new gate's* completeness — neither is a current inconsistency.

## Findings

**F-A — MEDIUM — the "class gate" covers 2 of 8 families that carry sha-pinning `artifact_refs`. `committed_source_universe_artifact_refs_match_current_reference_bytes` (artifact_refs.rs:42-76).**
The gate walks only `source-universe-execution-pack.json` and `source-universe-execution-acceptance-ledger.json`. I enumerated every committed reference JSON: **31 sha-pinning refs across 6 other families are ungated** — object-manifests, archive-index-manifests, conversion-queues, conversion-run-plans, object-gates, and operator-inputs. Concretely, operator-inputs and conversion-run-plans both pin `source_universe_object_gates`.
*Failure scenario:* the PR's own **deferred F2** (canonicalize the 4 trailing-newline Binance stragglers) will change the object-gates/queue/run-plan bytes → their shas. The gate will catch the stale pins in the pack + ledger (forcing lockstep updates) but will **silently miss** the stale `object_gates` pins inside the Binance operator-inputs and run-plan files → F2 ships a fresh stale-pin inconsistency, green — the exact class this gate exists to prevent, one family over. The fix is *cheaper* than the current code, not more: replace the two typed family-walks (`ExecutionPackRefs`/`AcceptanceLedgerRefs`) with one generic recursive walk over all reference JSON checking every `{role,path,sha256}`. I verified this is safe — all 31 ungated refs resolve to committed-or-indexed paths; **zero** point anywhere the walk couldn't resolve.

**F-B — LOW — evicted-branch is not three-way-closed for the 2 work-order refs. `check_artifact_ref` (artifact_refs.rs:97-101).**
For evicted paths the gate asserts `recorded == index`. Of the 4 evicted refs in packs/ledgers, pmxt-queue and bybit-run-plan are separately reproduction-checked (`regenerated.content_hash == index` in conversion_queue/execution_acceptance), but the **binance + bybit `conversion-work-order`** refs have no reproduction test binding index→regenerated bytes.
*Failure scenario:* a work-order fixture whose EvictedFixtureIndex entry is stale (≠ what its generator produces) would pass the gate as long as the recorded pin also matches the stale index — undetectable because the file is evicted. Pre-existing (no work-order reproduction test ever existed) and inherent to evicted fixtures; note as a tracked limitation rather than fix-now.

*(Pre-registered miss — `..._materializes_every_pmxt_archive_index_object_without_sha256_claim` name — acknowledged, not re-reported. I scanned the other `without_/no_sha/claim`-named tests: only that one now asserts a sha; no additional misnomers.)*

## Verified correct (per guarantee)

- **F1 fully closed.** Pack's `source_universe_operator_inputs` ref `8df9e1f9→81886b67` (exactly 1 line); ledger's `source_universe_execution_pack` ref `f9b99586→1af32501`. The cascade is exact: `sha256(pack@head) = 1af32501` = the ledger's new record (computed). `8df9e1f9` is **fully purged** repo-wide. Two pinning fields, as declared. ✔
- **Minimal-edit deviation is justified.** The committed `source-universe-execution-pack.toml` has no `record_limit`; only 3 `runs/*` files are committed for a 2,035-record pack — regenerating would regrow thousands of evicted `runs/*` artifacts. The pack has **no self-digest/content_hash field** (top-level keys checked), so the 1-line hand-edit breaks no pack-internal invariant; its external pin (the ledger) was updated in lockstep. ✔
- **The gate is genuinely differential.** Red at `3e963dbb` (`28711599503`) quoting the exact stale pack ref, green at head — the coverage it *does* have is real; it is read-only (no tree writes) and registered in tests.rs. ✔
- **FIX 3 complete + fail-loud preserved.** Zero `indexed_evicted_sha256` definitions/calls remain; all 5 sites delegate to `EvictedFixtureIndex::sha256_for`; the 3 TIER1 callers keep `.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(…))`, identical fail-loud to the old helper; new methods have a unit test. ✔
- **FIX 4 real.** `committed_bybit_…_track_current_gates` now keeps `run_plan_ref.path = TIER1…` but the `run_plan_ref.sha256 = …` overwrite is gone — the generator-stamped sha now flows into `normalized == committed`, so a mis-stamped run-plan sha would fail (was masked before). ✔
- **Round-1 guarantees hold at this head.** No changed test writes into `specs/023/reference/`; the 4 remaining trailing-newline stragglers stay consistent with the gate (recorded shas were computed on the with-newline bytes; the gate hashes current bytes → match) — and the gate correctly *locks in* that lockstep, going red if F2 strips a newline without updating the pack/ledger pin. ✔

## Recommendation

The round-1 blocker is resolved and the four fixes are sound — this is approvable on F1. But the gate should **not** be described as closing the class yet: it covers 2 of 8 sha-pinning families, and the deferred F2 straggler-canonicalization lands squarely in the ungated ones. My recommendation: **fold F-A (generalize the gate to all reference JSON — fewer lines, verified safe) and F-B (work-order index reproduction) into the same tracked F2 follow-up, and generalize the gate *before* F2's byte changes land** so F2 can't reintroduce a stale pin. If you'd rather ship round-2 as-is and broaden the gate inside F2, that's defensible provided F-A is explicitly on the F2 ledger, not silently dropped.

## Summary

This PR keeps source-universe generator tests from rewriting committed reference artifacts in-place. The committed-spec cases now copy specs into temp output roots, regenerate there, and compare generated bytes or evicted-index hashes against the committed reference surface.

It also refreshes the committed Binance operator-input artifact, aligns the execution-pack and acceptance-ledger artifact refs, and adds a generalized class gate that checks committed SHA pins across every reference JSON under `specs/023-nt-research-analytics-platform/reference/`.

## Root Cause

Some committed-spec tests invoked `write_*_from_spec_file` against the repository specs directly. Those specs pointed at committed reference output directories, so test execution could mutate tracked artifacts before later acceptance checks read them.

Round 2 found the same class in a stale `artifact_refs` pin: the Binance execution pack still recorded the old operator-input SHA after the operator-input artifact and acceptance ledger moved.

## Summary

This PR keeps source-universe generator tests from rewriting committed reference artifacts in-place. The committed-spec cases now copy specs into temp output roots, regenerate there, and compare generated bytes or evicted-index hashes against the committed reference surface.

It also refreshes the committed Binance operator-input artifact, aligns the execution-pack and acceptance-ledger artifact refs, and adds a generalized class gate that checks committed SHA pins across every reference JSON under `specs/023-nt-research-analytics-platform/reference/`.

## Root Cause

Some committed-spec tests invoked `write_*_from_spec_file` against the repository specs directly. Those specs pointed at committed reference output directories, so test execution could mutate tracked artifacts before later acceptance checks read them.

Round 2 found the same class in a stale `artifact_refs` pin: the Binance execution pack still recorded the old operator-input SHA after the operator-input artifact and acceptance ledger moved.

Round 3 found the gate was still too narrow: the typed pack/ledger walks did not cover other JSON pinning families such as object gates, operator inputs, conversion queues, run plans, manifests, and `committed_input_hashes`-style blocks.

Round 4 found two more pin shapes the generalized gate did not match yet: named `{path, sha256}` objects without a `role` field and flat sibling `*_path` plus `*_sha256` or `*_hash` pairs.

Round 5 corrected the reconciliation method: the affected execution packs were restored to canonical raw UTF-8 bytes, then updated with surgical SHA value substitution so the only content changes are the `execution_plan_sha256` pins and lockstep pack/ledger SHAs.

**Range:** head `a957df88e` vs round-3 baseline `2d5dad33b` (and vs merge-base `f57df191`). **CI verified live** (not trusted): run `28729300054` (CI, `workflow_dispatch`) and `28729300154` (Backtester CI, `workflow_dispatch`) both `success` at exactly `a957df88e`; red proofs `2ac3a93eb` (round‑3) and `13efdfe88` (round‑4) both real `failure`s. `verify-remote` non‑zero is the known queue‑only‑`gate` artifact.

My round-3 **F-1 is closed and proven by red proof**. One real finding remains, and it's the one the user's standard cares about most: the PR reconciles the *data* toward the index but leaves the *generator* emitting the hash identity that caused the drift. Not a blocker for the gate; it's a class-vs-instance gap. Reporting for triage — not declaring merge-ready.

## Findings

**F1 — MEDIUM — root cause of the 7,890-pin drift is unfixed; only the data was reconciled. `source_universe_execution_pack.rs:435` + `backfill_execution_plan.rs:473`/`:528`.**
The pack pins `execution_plan_sha256: execution_plan_artifact.content_hash`, and `content_hash` = `sha256_hex(serde_json::to_vec(plan))` — **compact**. But the evicted file is written **pretty** (`to_vec_pretty`, `:443`) and the index records the pretty file bytes. That compact-vs-pretty gap *is* the systematic cause the PR body correctly diagnoses. Round 5 reconciles the 7,890 committed pin values to the pretty/index hashes (correct target), **but the generator still emits `content_hash` (compact)** — so the committed reference and its own generator now disagree.
*Failure scenario:* regenerate either pack (add `record_limit`, or rebuild the evicted corpus) → the generator writes `execution_plan_sha256 = content_hash` (compact) for all 7,890 runs → they mismatch the index again → the class gate this PR adds goes red, requiring another hand-reconciliation. The instance (this cycle's stale data) is fixed; the class (generator produces the wrong hash identity) is not.
*Concrete fix, and it's local — not coupled to the deferred regeneration:* the write fn already has the pretty `bytes` in hand; return `content_hash: sha256_hex(&bytes)` (mirroring `read_accepted_tranche_manifest`'s `sha256_hex(&bytes)` two functions below) instead of re-serializing compact — or add a distinct file-byte field and pin that if `content_hash`'s compact semantics are consumed elsewhere (worth a grep before choosing). *Mitigation that lowers this from High:* the new class gate converts the latent generator bug from **silent stale pins** to a **loud gate failure** on any regeneration — so the "uncaught drift" class genuinely is closed; what's open is the generator still emitting the value that trips it. If you defer the generator fix, it must be tracked as the explicit root-cause/class-closure item, not treated as closed by the data reconciliation.

**F2 — LOW — broadened `artifact_ref_from_object` accepts bare `{path, sha256}` with any syntactically-valid path as a live pin. `artifact_refs.rs` `artifact_ref_from_object`.**
Round 4/5 relaxed the object matcher: an object with `path`+`sha256` and no `role` is treated as a pin whenever `normalize_repo_path(path)` succeeds. `normalize_repo_path` only rejects empty/`://`/absolute/`..` — it accepts arbitrary strings like `"human description"` as "valid."
*Failure scenario:* a future reference JSON adds an object whose `path` field is a label/description (not a real repo path) alongside an unrelated `sha256` → the gate mis-collects it as a pin, hashes a nonexistent file → `<unreadable>` mismatch → gate red on unrelated content. No live instance (0 mismatches at head; 0 invalid paths), so latent. The role-required object shape from round 3 didn't have this latitude.

**F3 — LOW — the source-attestation exclusion is keyed on the `-status.` filename infix only. `artifact_refs.rs` `is_dated_status_file`.**
`should_enforce` skips a pin only when the owner filename matches `*-status.YYYY-MM-DD.json` *and* the target is `crates/|src/|scripts/`. The unit test deliberately leaves an `-audit.2026-06-09.json` dated file's source pin **enforced**.
*Failure scenario:* a future point-in-time source attestation written under any other dated convention (e.g. `-audit.DATE.json`) is enforced against current source bytes → churns red every time that source file is edited, reintroducing exactly the false-positive the exclusion exists to prevent. No live instance today (0 enforced source-tree pins in the tree), so latent naming-coupling, not a current defect.

## Verified guarantees (per-guarantee, with reasoning)

**Census (item 1) — clean, byte-reproduced.** Round-3→round-5 touches exactly 4 files: gate test (±199), 2 packs, 1 ledger. In the packs+ledger the *only* changed lines are **7,890** `execution_plan_sha256` values (2034 binance + 5856 bybit) + **2** ledger `sha256` lockstep pins — every one of the 7,890 matches a strict `"key": "<64-hex>",` template (no indent/key/comma drift), symmetric del==add, and the 2 ledger pins equal the actual current pack sha256 (`1a9c0045…`, `2a812905…`). **Zero** `\uXXXX` escapes, **zero** structural/non-key changed lines. Round-4's non-canonical re-encoding is fully gone. The `+153` line-count asymmetry in `--stat` is entirely the `.rs` gate test (176+23=199), not pack content.

**Cause narrative (item 2) — proven, not asserted; code-anchored end-to-end.** `pack.execution_plan_sha256` ← `artifact.content_hash` (`:435`) ← `content_hash(plan)` = compact `to_vec` (`:473→528`); file written pretty (`:443`); index = pretty file bytes. Empirically: all 2034 binance evicted pins now == index; the 1 retained `runs/00000` == its on-disk file; 0 mismatches tree-wide. "Why 100%" (systematic serialization gap) and "why index side" (file-byte-addressed surface; consumers verify downloaded pretty bytes) both hold. The one piece I could *not* independently recompute is the prior compact values (plan objects are evicted) — that side rests on code + git history, which the body states honestly.

**Source-path exclusion (item 3) — exactly narrow, not foolable.** Replicating the gate over the HEAD tree: **24,515** pins collected = **24,513 enforced + 2 skipped** (matches the body's count). The 2 skipped are both in `source-proof-…-status.2026-06-16.json` → `crates/.../src/source_proof_admissibility.rs` and `.../src/source_proof.rs` — genuine point-in-time attestations. **0 reference-tree pins skipped** and **0 enforced source-tree pins** (no leak). By construction no `specs/…/reference/…` target can be `is_source_tree_path` (prefixes are `crates/|src/|scripts/` only), so no reproducibility pin is ever exempted. `should_enforce` runs on the *normalized* path (after `normalize_repo_path` strips `repo://` and rejects `..`/absolute/`://`; 0 invalid at head), so `../`/absolute/`repo://` forms can't sneak a reference target into the skip branch. It's a structural class rule (naming + prefix), not an instance hardcode, and the doc comment documents it. This is correct scoping (kills false positives), not a fence-as-fix — the behavioral fix (temp-redirect) lives in the round-1 test changes.

**Prior-round guarantees (item 4) — all hold.**
- **F1 (round 1):** `8df9e1f9…` fully purged (0 occurrences); operator-inputs pin consistent (part of the 0-mismatch set). ✓
- **F-A (round 2):** gate coverage now maximal — object, role-less named object, flat-sibling `*_path`+`*_sha256`/`*_hash`, and `committed_input_hashes` (via inferred role). ✓
- **FIX 3 / FIX 4 (round 2):** not in the round-5 delta (only gate + 2 packs + ledger changed), so `EvictedFixtureIndex::sha256_for`/`entry_for` and the bybit overwrite removal are intact. ✓

The generic matcher closes the whole class (0 mismatch across all flat siblings). ✓
- **F-2 (my round 3):** work-order eviction limitation now explicitly documented for both chains with "derived from pre-eviction git history, not repo-verifiable bytes." Honest doc-scope note. ✓

# PR #1222 — Round 6 (final) review: root-cause fix + carry-over

**Range:** head `b496f841e` vs round-5 `a957df88e` (delta = 2 `.rs` files, **zero JSON**). **CI verified live:** `28730645954` (CI) + `28730646429` (Backtester) both `success` at `b496f841e`; red proof `28730630014` `failure` at scratch `5c8acdceb`.

**Bottom line:** the execution_plan fix itself is exactly right and I verified it end-to-end — correct hash, helper deleted, non-vacuous red-proven test, zero data churn, no consumer breakage. But checklist item 3 — "is the *class* closed?" — comes back **no**. The identical compact-hash-of-a-pretty-file defect lives in ~15 other `write_*` functions. Round 6 fixed the instance. Reporting for triage; not declaring merge-ready.

## Finding

**F1 — MEDIUM — the class is not closed; ~15 sibling `write_*` functions still record a compact `content_hash` for a pretty-written file. `crates/backtesting-vertical-slice/src/backfill_*.rs` + `source_proof_*.rs`.**
The bug round 6 fixed was: write `bytes = to_vec_pretty(x)` + `atomic_write`, then record `content_hash: content_hash(x)` where `content_hash()` re-serializes **compact** `to_vec(x)`. That exact shape survives in every one of these write functions (confirmed: `backfill_conversion_batch::write_backfill_conversion_batch_plan` records `content_hash: content_hash(plan)?` while writing `bytes` pretty — byte-for-byte the pre-round-6 execution_plan bug; contrast `source_universe_object_gates` which correctly records `sha256_hex(&bytes)`):

`backfill_accepted_tranche` (+ its `source_proof_scope_report_hash`), `backfill_binding_coverage`, `backfill_conversion_batch`, `backfill_conversion_completion`, `backfill_execution_readiness`, `backfill_preflight`, `backfill_readiness`, `backfill_source_proof_scope`, `backfill_object_staging` (inline `manifest_hash`), `source_proof_evidence_staging` (inline `manifest_hash`), `source_catalog_mapping_readiness`, `source_proof_migration_preflight`, `source_proof_shortlist`, `source_selection_readiness`, `first_proof_selector` (both `content_hash` and `event_count_ledger_report_hash`).

*Tell that these are bugs, not intentional logical identities:* each returns `content_hash` alongside `bytes: bytes.len()` — the length describes the pretty file, the hash describes a different (compact) serialization, so the artifact descriptor is internally inconsistent. The correct modules (execution_plan post-fix + the whole `source_universe_*` family) make `path`/`bytes`/`content_hash` all describe the same written bytes.
*Failure scenario:* identical to execution_plan's. These are **latent today** — I re-confirmed 0 active mismatches across all 24,513 pins (round 6 changed no JSON), so none of these content_hashes are currently pinned in the gate-checked surface. But the moment any of these artifacts is evicted/pinned and the generalized gate walks its pin, it's stale by the same compact-vs-pretty mechanism — the silent-until-surfaced trap that took this PR six rounds to close for one module.
*Class fix (mechanical, already the codebase's own convention):* make every `write_*` record `sha256_hex(&bytes)` and delete the compact `content_hash()`/inline helpers — the transform round 6 applied once. If the backfill pipeline is separately owned and out of this PR's scope, then track it as an explicit class-closure ledger item with this enumerated list — don't let the single-module fix stand in for the class.

## Verified guarantees (per-guarantee, with reasoning)

**The instance fix (correctness) — looks fine.** `content_hash: content_hash(plan)?` → `content_hash: sha256_hex(&bytes)` hashes the exact pretty `bytes` written via `atomic_write`; the compact `content_hash()` helper is deleted entirely (no dangling refs — it was the only caller). This is precisely the fix I specified in round 5.

**Item 1 — consumer census — clean.** Crate-wide, `BackfillExecutionPlanArtifact`/`.content_hash` is referenced in only 3 files: the producer, the pin at `source_universe_execution_pack.rs:435` (now correctly file-bytes), and the tests. The idempotence test (`assert_eq!(first.content_hash, second.content_hash)`) is semantics-agnostic (equality of two identical writes). No consumer recomputes a compact hash for comparison or hardcodes a compact value — so nothing relies on the old semantics. Step-0 census confirmed.

**Item 2 — data neutrality — confirmed.** Zero JSON changed round-5→round-6. Both retained `runs/00000` pins equal `sha256` of their on-disk pretty file under the new code (binance `dd82ea85…`, bybit `07171b2e…` — MATCH), so the fixed generator agrees with the round-5 reconciled data. The evicted counts reconcile (2034 + 5856 = 7890).

**Item 4 — the new test — non-vacuous and red-proven.** `retained_execution_plan_artifact_hash_matches_written_file_bytes` reads the retained binance plan, regenerates to a temp dir, and asserts `content_hash == hex(Sha256(on-disk written bytes))`. Scratch `5c8acdceb` = this new test on the **old** source (src diff shows the old `content_hash(plan)`; test diff is empty) → red proof `28730630014` failed there. It can't pass vacuously: on old code compact≠pretty for a non-trivial plan; on new code they're equal by construction. *Caveat (fair to note):* it exercises only the retained plan — the 7,890 evicted plans can't be regenerated without regrowing the corpus, so their correctness rests on the shared code path plus the round-5 index reconciliation, not a live regeneration. Reasonable under the eviction policy.

**Item 5 — carry-over — holds.** The gate-scoping test (`..._source_universe_artifact_refs.rs`) is unchanged (empty diff), so my round-5 verification of the exclusion (exactly 2 source-attestation pins skipped, 0 reference-tree skipped, path-form-safe) carries over intact. The round-5 census holds trivially (0 JSON changed). The body's ledger records my round-5 F2 (bare `{path,sha256}` latitude) and F3 (`-status`-only keying), plus a third they surfaced (`normalize_repo_path` doesn't strip a leading `./`) — all deferred to the canonical-writer / Brief 9 ledger.

Merits: the execution_plan root-cause fix is correct, minimal, deletes the offending helper, is guarded by a differential red-proven test, changes no committed bytes, and breaks no consumer — every specific guarantee checks out. The single open item is F1: item 3 explicitly asked whether the *class* is closed, and it isn't — the same defect sits in ~15 enumerated sibling `write_*` functions (latent now, gate green, but the identical trap).
